item.title: La Vagabonde
item.description:
Colette’s La Vagabonde, in the Cheyne Éditeur edition (2025, copy no. 158/425), was given a full binding in black epi goatskin, embellished with fine gold chains that fall from the boards as the book opens.

Inside, pink calfskin doublures are embossed with handwriting and a signature, facing grey flyleaves; the headband is embroidered. The spine is titled La Vagabonde. Gold tooling by Geneviève de Boiry.

Presented at the 18th Biennale Mondiale de la Reliure d’Art, this binding received the Technical Excellence Award from the jury.

item.title: Le Club des Lyonnais
item.description:
Georges Duhamel’s Le Club des Lyonnais, published by Albert Guillot in 1950 (copy no. 903), is illustrated in colour. It was given a full binding in tan Oasis goatskin with raised bands and a titled spine.

Inside, the doublures are lined with silk and framed by a leather listel, facing marbled paper flyleaves. The book is protected by a grey-lined chemise with a raised-band leather spine and blue marbled paper sides, which slides into a leather-edged slipcase. The marbled papers are by Thomas Braun.

item.title: La Peau de Chagrin
item.description:
Honoré de Balzac’s La Peau de Chagrin, in the 1947 Jacques Vautrain edition (copy no. 788), was given a three-piece Bradel binding.

The black epi goatskin boards carry inlays of dyed natural calfskin, and the calfskin spine is titled. The book is protected by a chemise and a black slipcase edged in calfskin, with a calfskin title tab. The title is a nod to the material: chagrin is the French name for the goatskin covering the boards.

item.title: Les Dernières Lettres
item.description:
Vincent van Gogh’s Les Dernières Lettres, published in 2023 by the Éditions du musée d’Orsay et du musée de l’Orangerie and Éditions Hazan, was given a floating spine binding.

The blue goatskin covers carry engraved leather inlays and a gold title; the yellow and green floating spine recalls the painter’s colours. The endpapers are yellow. The book is kept in a two-part yellow slipcase, titled on the spine.

item.title: Poèmes d'Enfance
item.description:
Anna de Noailles’s Poèmes d’Enfance (Anna de Brancovan, Countess de Noailles), published by Grasset in 1928, Alfa copy no. 391, was given a framed binding.

On each cover, a brown goatskin frame surrounds green decorated papers; the spine is tooled in gold. Inside, a brown flyleaf faces a decorated paper doublure. A chemise in green paper and goatskin, also titled in gold, and a matching slipcase complete the set. The papers are by Katalin Perry.

item.title: Avec Calder
item.description:
Daniel Lelong’s Avec Calder, published by L’Échoppe in 2000, became a creative binding in grey board: an accordion binding on guards, combined with a storage box for mobiles.

Unfolded, the accordion reveals windows and holds a colourful mobile, echoing the work of Alexander Calder. The built-in box keeps the mobiles with the book. Closed, the whole piece reads as a quiet volume with a titled grey board spine.

item.title: La Vie et Le Monde Du Boulevard (1830-1870)
item.description:
Paul d’Ariste’s La Vie et le Monde du Boulevard (1830-1870), published by Éditions Jules Tallandier in 1930, was given a three-piece Bradel binding.

The covers combine white goatskin and black box calf inlays in a geometric pattern that runs from the front cover across the titled spine to the back. In a three-piece Bradel binding the spine and the boards are covered separately and then assembled, which is what makes this crisp, graphic play of contrasting leathers possible.

item.title: About
item.description:
About Atelier Septain and Nami Lévy

Atelier Septain

Septain in French means a cord made of 7 strands of hemp fiber, often used in bookbinding of medieval era. Even though each strands are thin, when seven of them are twisted together, it becomes very strong cord, which holds books for hundreds of years. Atelier Septain was named because of my wish to create artifacts with strong quality which last for a long time by merging my various experiences and skills in different fields (book binding, graphic design, product design, case making, edition, and sewing).

item.title: Abécédaire de Mon Univers
item.description:
Anne-Lise Courchay’s Abécédaire de Mon Univers (2018), copy no. 007 of 180 signed by the author, was given an oriental binding with articulated boards in black calfskin.

A white alphabet runs across the covers; some letters, such as the O, are made of floral motifs. The boards are built from hinged panels that unfold on either side of the spine, so the book opens flat and the sewing stays visible inside. Closed, it shows a titled spine and a clean profile, leaving the contrast of white on black leather to speak for itself.

item.title: Journal with articulated cover boards
item.description:
This journal is a creative binding: a three-piece Bradel binding covered in turquoise cloth.

Its boards are articulated, so they fold as the journal opens. A pink endpaper appears as soon as it is opened, in contrast with the cloth. The journal shows how a traditional bookbinding technique, the Bradel binding, can shape an everyday object.

item.title: The Elements of Typographic Style
item.description:
Robert Bringhurst’s The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 2001, version 2.4), a reference work on typography, was given an exposed spine binding.

The black and white sewing stays visible on the spine and becomes part of the design; the parchment covers carry parchment inlays and the title. The book is kept in a box covered in grey veined paper with a triangular window. Leaving the structure visible suits a book about the form of text.

item.title: Les Après-Soupers
item.description:
Léon Jaybert’s Les Après-Soupers, published by Rouveyre et G. Blond in 1883 (copy no. 334/500 on laid paper), was given a full binding in blue-grey Oasis goatskin with raised bands and a titled spine.

The book is protected by a marbled paper chemise with a raised-band leather spine and by a pink and blue marbled paper slipcase by Sylvie Hournon. Opening the book reveals the illustrated title page.

item.title: GAUDI - an introduction to his architecture
item.description:
Juan-Eduardo Cirlot’s Gaudí, an introduction to his architecture (Triangle Postals, 2008) was given a piano hinge binding in white goatskin.

The covers carry colourful stingray leather inlays and a gold title; the piano hinge spine, in blue and yellow bands, joins the boards like a hinge. The colours and textures of the stingray leather recall the ceramics of Gaudí’s façades. The book is kept in a box with a white goatskin spine and grey striped paper, whose blue interior holds it in a tray.

item.title: Amélie
item.description:
Henri Troyat’s Amélie, published by Plon in 1955, was given a traditional half goatskin binding with bands.

Khaki goatskin covers the titled spine and forms bands on the boards, which are covered in blue decorated paper. In a half binding, leather protects the parts of the book that see the most wear while the paper gives the piece its character: a sturdy, elegant binding for a book that is meant to be read.

item.title: Le Chemin Étroit vers Les Contrées du Nord
item.description:
Matsuo Bashō’s Narrow Road to the Deep North, in Nicolas Bouvier’s French translation (Le Chemin étroit vers les contrées du Nord, Éditions Héros-Limite, 2006), is a paperback. It was protected with a chemise with fore-edge flaps and a slipcase, which keep it in its original state.

The chemise has a titled brown goatskin spine and is covered in brown marbled paper by Claude Braun; its inside is lined in gold and its flaps wrap around the book. The decorated paper slipcase holds the chemise. Gold tooling by Geneviève de Boiry.

item.title: Le Rêve
item.description:
Émile Zola’s Le Rêve, published by Les Éditions du Panthéon in 1947 (copy no. 1359/2500), is illustrated in colour. It was given a full binding in cream goatskin, dyed with a pink and blue geometric pattern that runs across the covers and spine.

The head of the book is grey, speckled with gold, and the spine is titled Le Rêve, Émile Zola. The book is kept in a grey paper slipcase. Papers by Katalin Perry.

item.title: Braque ou la Peinture Sacrée / Huit Entretiens Avec Picasso / Henri Matisse 1907-1918 / Klee, Point Final
item.description:
This project brings together four books published by L’Échoppe: Jean Paulhan’s Braque ou la peinture sacrée, Daniel-Henry Kahnweiler’s Huit entretiens avec Picasso, Guillaume Apollinaire’s Henri Matisse 1907-1918 and Antonio Saura’s Klee, point final.

Each book was given a cloth and paper binding in a different variation. The four volumes are gathered in a folding presentation board with a decorated spine, which slides into a grey cloth slipcase. Unfolded, the board shows the four books side by side.

item.title: Zazie dans le métro
item.description:
Raymond Queneau’s Zazie dans le métro (Gallimard, 1996) was a paperback, turned into a hardcover book with a three-piece Bradel binding.

The covers and spine are covered in green and yellow printed paper with metro motifs, and the title appears on the front cover. Inside, the original paperback cover is preserved. The conversion gives an ordinary paperback a second life, with a design that recalls the novel’s subject.

item.title: Madame Chrysanthème
item.description:
Pierre Loti’s Madame Chrysanthème, published by Calmann-Lévy in 1923, was given a half parchment Bradel binding with corners.

White parchment covers the spine and the corners; the boards are covered in blue and beige marbled paper by Thomas Braun, and a brown title label sits on the spine. The Bradel binding, light and elegant, suits this novel by Loti set in Japan.

item.title: Souvenirs from Japan
item.description:
Margarita Winkel’s Souvenirs from Japan (Bamboo Publishing, 1991) was given a half cloth binding with bands.

Grey cloth covers the spine, with a black title label, and forms bands on the boards, which are covered in grey and black marbled paper by Thomas Braun. Inside, a mauve fibrous endpaper comes before the illustrated title page.

item.title: Stéphanette
item.description:
René Bazin’s Stéphanette, published by Éditions Mame in 1930, came to the studio with a damaged original publisher’s binding: a worn spine and a damaged headcap.

The spine was stripped so the book could be reworked, and the original illustrated cover was lifted to be remounted. The book was then given a Bradel case binding that keeps the original covers: a blue cloth spine with a title label, and the original boards preserved. This restoration makes the book sound again while keeping its publisher’s decoration.

item.title: Cinq Nouvelles
item.description:
Henri Duvernois’s Cinq Nouvelles, published by Roger Dacosta in 1936, is illustrated with colour and pencil drawings. It was given a full olive goatskin binding whose covers and spine carry gold line drawings of nudes, with the title on the front cover.

The book is protected by a chemise with a goatskin spine and by a slipcase in blue and gold marbled paper, edged in blue. The marbled papers are by Marianne Peter.

item.title: Le Petit Prince
item.description:
Antoine de Saint-Exupéry’s Le Petit Prince (Gallimard, 2021) was given a full yellow cloth binding with a brown title label on the spine.

Inside, a blue and yellow marbled endpaper by Katalin Perry picks up the colours of the cloth. A simple, bright binding for a book that is read again and again.

item.title: La Cigale et la Fourmi
item.description:
Jean de La Fontaine’s La Cigale et la Fourmi is presented here as a creative accordion binding, covered in green cloth with an illustrated title label.

Unfolded, the pages form an illustrated frieze: a spread with a caption and a yellow sun, others in ochre or grey tones, and one with grey clouds and a round cut-out. The accordion format lets the reader follow the fable page by page or see it fully unfolded.

item.title: Une Vie
item.description:
Guy de Maupassant’s Une Vie, published by Albin Michel in 1925, was given a Romantic-style half goatskin binding with corners and raised bands.

Green goatskin covers the corners and the raised-band spine, titled in gold; the boards are covered in orange and green marbled paper by Katalin Perry. The Romantic style, inspired by 19th-century bindings, suits this novel first published in 1883.

item.title: Sommeil
item.description:
Haruki Murakami’s Sommeil (Éditions 10/18, 2011) was given a black quarter goatskin binding.

The spine is titled Sommeil and the boards are covered in black and white wave-patterned marbled paper by Brigitte Chardonne. Inside, a marbled endpaper comes before the original cover, kept within the binding. The wave-patterned paper echoes the mood of the story.

item.title: Colline
item.description:
Jean Giono’s Colline, published by Grasset in 1942, was given a traditional half goatskin binding with corners.

Green goatskin covers the spine and the corners, and the boards are covered in blue and gold marbled paper. A half binding with corners protects the parts of a book most exposed to wear, the spine and the corners, and lets the marbled paper set the tone. Giono’s first novel, Colline was bound in the same edition as Un de Baumugnes.

item.title: Un de Baumugnes
item.description:
Jean Giono’s Un de Baumugnes, published by Grasset in 1942, was given a half goatskin binding with bands.

Green goatskin covers the spine and forms bands on the boards, which are covered in blue and green marbled paper by Sylvie Hournon, its colours answering the green of the leather. By the same author and in the same edition, the studio also bound Colline.

item.title: La Vie Privée d'Autrefois
item.description:
Alfred Franklin’s La Vie privée d’autrefois, published by Plon in 1888, was given a half goatskin binding with corners and raised bands.

Green goatskin covers the corners and the titled raised-band spine; the boards are covered in orange and green marbled paper by Sylvie Hournon. This classic half binding with raised bands suits a book from the late 19th century.

item.title: Journal with flexible wood cover
item.description:
This journal is a creative binding with flexible wood veneer covers, made with the method taught by bookbinder Dominique Dumont.

The covers combine light wood with a band of dark wood; the rounded spine is veneer too. The thinness of the wood sheets keeps the cover flexible. Inside, the endpapers are brown.
